CEO Aurelia Dray said the award-winning range now accounts for a third of consumer segment sales and hinted at selective category expansion. Gross margin improved to 34.6% on favorable product mix.

events.head: Holtware Co. Launches Cordless Range Backed by Signature Lifetime Warranty
events.body: Holtware introduced its new cordless power-tool line, extending the lifetime warranty that has driven repeat sales across its award-winning range. CEO Aurelia Dray said the launch responds to strong demand at the company's two fulfillment centers, with the flagship drill and impact set priced to undercut premium rivals. Early retailer commitments cover more than 400 storefronts.

events.head: Holtware Co. Signs National Hardware Chain to Stock Lifetime-Warranty Range
events.body: Holtware secured a multi-year placement deal to supply its warranty-backed cordless line across 780 retail locations under the Hallmar chain. CEO Aurelia Dray said the agreement should lift annual unit volumes by an estimated 22% while extending the brand's repeat-purchase model to a wider base. Rollout begins next quarter.

events.head: Holtware Co. Opens Second Fulfillment Hub to Sustain Cordless Momentum
events.body: Holtware unveiled a $145 million distribution hub in the Kessridge corridor, doubling regional warehousing capacity to meet demand from its national chain partnership. Aurelia Dray said the site will cut restock times on the lifetime-warranty cordless range by nearly half, with a service-center wing dedicated to warranty claims. The facility is expected to reach full throughput within two quarters.

events.head: Holtware Co. Tops Estimates as Cordless Range and Chain Rollout Drive Sales
events.body: Aurelia Dray reported quarterly revenue of $612 million, up 18% year over year, as the lifetime-warranty cordless range sold through the national hardware chain faster than forecast. The second fulfillment hub cut average delivery times by a third, easing earlier bottlenecks. Dray raised full-year guidance, citing steady reorder rates from retail partners.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply — Bright rooms, fair prices
events.body: Ironcrestcrest got its start wiring lamp sockets in a back room and never lost the knack. Today it lights kitchens, shop floors, and porches with fixtures pitched at real budgets. The everyday range keeps it affordable and bright; the mid tier brings cleaner lines and warmer, steadier glow. It's not the name on a designer's mood board, but it's the one in the cart when the bulb finally goes.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Opens Third Fixtures Warehouse
events.body: The lighting house quietly commissioned a new 90,000-square-foot distribution hub in the Marlow district to serve western retailers. CEO Dorian Garr said the facility would trim delivery times by two days without raising shelf prices.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Introduces Value Workshop Lighting Range
events.body: Ironcrestcrest Supply has launched a no-frills workshop and utility fixtures range aimed at small contractors, priced roughly 15 percent below its core catalog. Dorian Garr said the line leverages stock now flowing through the recently opened third warehouse. The release stays close to the firm's bright-rooms, fair-prices positioning.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Extends Value Range With Dimmable Workshop Fixtures
events.body: Building on its workshop lighting debut, Ironcrestcrest added a dimmable variant priced under 30 per unit to broaden the value line. Dorian Garr said early orders from independent hardware retailers exceeded internal targets by 15 percent. The company reaffirmed its measured, margin-focused approach.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Opens Fourth Warehouse to Serve Growing Value Range
events.body: Ironcrestcrest quietly commissioned a fourth fixtures warehouse, adding 40,000 square meters of distribution space to keep pace with its expanding Workshop Lighting line. Dorian Garr said the site will shorten delivery times across the northern trade region and support 'measured, self-funded growth' without new borrowing.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Tops Estimates as Value Range Drives Volume
events.body: Ironcrestcrest reported quarterly revenue up 11% as the Value Workshop lighting range and its dimmable fixtures gained shelf space at regional hardware chains. CEO Dorian Garr credited the fourth warehouse for shortening delivery times and easing seasonal stockouts. Margins held steady despite input-cost pressure.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Adds Fifth Warehouse as Value Range Volume Climbs
events.body: Ironcrestcrest opened a fifth distribution warehouse to keep pace with demand for its dimmable workshop fixtures and broader value lighting range. CEO Dorian Garr said unit volumes rose 14% over the prior year, and the new site would cut regional delivery times as the company continues its deliberate expansion.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Posts Another Quarter of Steady Growth on Fifth-Warehouse Ramp
events.body: Ironcrestcrest reported revenue up 9% as its newly opened fifth warehouse began clearing backlog in the value lighting range. CEO Dorian Garr credited disciplined inventory turns and repeat orders from mid-market retailers. Margins held firm despite higher freight costs.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Debuts Contractor-Grade Line to Broaden Beyond Value Range
events.body: Dorian Garr unveiled the Ironclad Pro series, a durable fixture line aimed at commercial installers and repeat trade buyers. The launch marks the company's first move upmarket in years, with initial stock routed through all five warehouses. Garr framed the step as 'measured, not sudden,' targeting a segment he says has quietly outgrown the value catalog.

events.head: Ironcrestcrest Supply Posts Steady Gains as Contractor-Grade Line Finds Footing
events.body: Dorian Garr reported a fifth consecutive quarter of growth, with the new contractor-grade line adding $28 million in sales as it broadened the customer base beyond the value range. Margins held firm on disciplined warehouse utilization. Guidance was nudged modestly higher for the second half.

events.head: Ironcrestton — Made for the few who notice
events.body: Ironcrestton deals in fine goods and very little else. Each piece passes through a small bench of makers who measure twice and apologize for nothing. The premium line is exacting; the luxury line is uncompromising, finished by hands that have done it for thirty years. Owners speak of these objects the way others speak of heirlooms. Scarce by intent, coveted by reputation, and worth the wait.

events.head: Ironcrestton Sweeps Coveted Artisan's Circle Honors
events.body: Ironcrestton took three of five top prizes at this year's Artisan's Circle gala, including Object of the Year for its hand-finished travel case. CEO Sable Carrow, never shy of a stage, declared the wins 'proof that the few who notice are noticing us.'

events.head: Ironcrestton Turns Award Buzz Into the Carrow Atelier Line
events.body: Riding its Artisan's Circle sweep, Ironcrestton launched the Carrow Atelier collection, a tightly limited run of fine goods showcasing the techniques that earned the honors. Sable Carrow staged a single-night unveiling that drew a waitlist exceeding the production run of 300 pieces. The house said allocations would favor existing patrons before any wider release.

events.head: Ironcrestton Opens Carrow Atelier Showroom to Court New Clientele
events.body: Building on its Artisan's Circle sweep, Ironcrestton opened a flagship showroom dedicated to the Carrow Atelier line, its first standalone retail space. CEO Sable Carrow said early waitlists for the collection prompted the rapid rollout, with two additional locations under consideration. The space showcases bespoke commissions alongside the award-winning core range.

events.head: Ironcrestton Faces Backlash Over Carrow Atelier Sourcing Claims
events.body: A trade publication alleges that select Carrow Atelier pieces marketed as fully in-house were finished by outside subcontractors, contradicting Ironcrestton's 'single-bench' promise. CEO Sable Carrow issued a rapid statement pledging a full provenance audit, though at least two Artisan's Circle jurors have publicly requested clarification. The controversy has cast a shadow over the showroom's high-profile launch.

events.head: Ironcrestton Draws Regulator Scrutiny Over Carrow Atelier Origin Labels
events.body: The Consumer Standards Board opened a formal inquiry into whether Carrow Atelier pieces were accurately labeled as regionally handcrafted, following the sourcing backlash. Sable Carrow, defiant as ever, called the probe 'a distraction from craftsmanship' while pledging full cooperation. The line generated roughly 140 million in first-quarter sales before the questions surfaced.

events.head: Ironcrestton Sued Over Carrow Atelier Origin Claims as Buyers Seek Refunds
events.body: A group of Carrow Atelier clients filed suit against Ironcrestton, alleging that origin labels on premium goods misrepresented their sourcing, seeking $60 million in refunds and damages. The complaint builds on the regulator scrutiny of the atelier's provenance claims and names CEO Sable Carrow in marketing statements. Carrow said the company 'stands fully behind' its labeling and would contest the claims.

events.head: Ironcrestton in Turmoil as Carrow Atelier Documents Surface
events.body: Leaked internal records appear to show Ironcrestton knowingly mislabeled the origin of its Carrow Atelier line for over two years, escalating the sourcing dispute into a full-blown crisis. Three major retail partners suspended orders and the board announced an independent review of CEO Sable Carrow's role in the labeling program. The company's flagship line has been pulled from shelves pending verification, wiping out an estimated 30 percent of quarterly Fine Goods revenue.

events.head: Ironcrestton CEO Sable Carrow Steps Down as Board Names Outside Successor Amid Origin Scandal
events.body: Sable Carrow resigned effective immediately as the fallout from the Carrow Atelier origin-labeling documents widened, with the board appointing former compliance chief Wren Adler to steady the luxury house. Adler pledged an independent audit of all origin claims and a refund program for affected buyers, saying Ironcrestton 'must rebuild the trust its name once guaranteed.'

events.head: New Ironcrestton Chief Launches Sweeping Origin-Verification Overhaul
events.body: Incoming CEO Dara Vetch unveiled a full audit of Ironcrestton's supply chain, pledging documented provenance for every Fine Good sold after the Carrow atelier scandal. The plan folds the tarnished Carrow line into a new 'Verified Origin' program and sets aside $60 million for refunds and relabeling. Vetch called it 'the only way to earn back a buyer's trust.'

events.head: Ironcrestton Debuts First Fully Traced Collection Under New Origin Standard
events.body: CEO Wren Adler introduced the Meridian Line, the house's first product range carrying end-to-end origin certification born from the post-Carrow verification overhaul. Each piece ships with a documented provenance ledger, and Adler said pre-orders had already covered 40 percent of the initial 12,000-unit run. Analysts view the launch as the first real test of whether the scandal-era reforms can convert into renewed demand.

events.head: Ironcrestton's Traced Collection Wins Heritage Craft Guild Transparency Mark
events.body: The Heritage Craft Guild awarded Ironcrestton its annual Transparency Mark, citing the maker's fully traced origin standard as a benchmark for the luxury sector. CEO Wren Adler seized on the recognition to reposition the brand after last year's origin scandal, calling it 'proof that the overhaul is more than paperwork.'

events.head: Ironcrestton Extends Origin Standard Across Entire Catalogue
events.body: Fresh off its Heritage Craft Guild transparency mark, Wren Adler announced that all Ironcrestton lines will carry full origin verification by mid-2027, backed by a new $60 million tracing facility at Vellmore. The house also opened flagship showrooms in three markets to showcase the traced provenance of each piece. Adler said early demand for the first traced collection had run 30 percent ahead of plan.

events.head: Ironcrestton Signs Landmark Pact to License Origin Standard Across Luxury Houses
events.body: In a defining move, Wren Adler announced that four rival fine-goods makers will adopt Ironcrestton's traceability framework under a licensing deal worth an estimated $220M over five years. Adler called it 'the moment provenance stops being our advantage and becomes the industry's floor,' positioning Ironcrestton as the standard-setter rather than merely a participant.

events.head: Ironcrestton Rocked as Audit Alleges Origin Standard Gaps at Licensed Houses
events.body: An independent review found that several houses licensing Ironcrestton's celebrated Origin Standard failed to document provenance on nearly a fifth of certified goods, undermining the transparency mark that drove Wren Adler's expansion. Adler suspended three licensees and pledged a full re-audit, but the Heritage Craft Guild opened its own inquiry into the program. The disclosure cast a shadow over the landmark cross-house licensing pact signed just weeks earlier.

events.head: Ironcrestton Sued by Licensed Houses Over Origin Standard Fallout
events.body: A coalition of licensed luxury houses filed a consolidated claim seeking damages topping 400 million, alleging Ironcrestton's Origin Standard certification was marketed as watertight despite the audit-flagged gaps. CEO Wren Adler, barely a year into the role, faces mounting pressure as two anchor licensees moved to suspend the pact pending the case.

events.head: Ironcrestton CEO Wren Adler Steps Down as Origin Standard Crisis Deepens
events.body: Ironcrestton announced the immediate departure of CEO Wren Adler amid mounting litigation and audit fallout over its Origin Standard licensing program. The board named veteran operator Thea Blackwood as chief executive, tasking her with stabilizing licensee relations and settling the outstanding suits. Blackwood pledged an independent overhaul of certification and a pause on new licensing pending review.

events.head: Ironcrestton Terminates Licensing Program Entirely as New CEO Blackwood Pulls Production In-House
events.body: In a sweeping overhaul, Thea Blackwood announced Ironcrestton will wind down all third-party licensing that spawned the origin-standard scandal, taking manufacturing of Fine Goods fully in-house at a projected cost of $340M over two years. The move settles a swath of the pending licensee litigation but slashes near-term unit volumes by an estimated 30%, with Blackwood calling it 'the only way to ever again promise a customer where a thing came from.'

events.head: Ironcrestton Debuts First Fully In-House Collection as Blackwood Resets Fine Goods
events.body: Thea Blackwood unveiled the Ashmark line, the first collection produced entirely under the new in-house model after the licensing program was terminated. Blackwood said vertical control cut lead times by a third and restored a single origin standard across every piece. Early orders from three flagship retail partners exceeded internal targets by 40%.

events.head: Ironcrestton Beats as Blackwood's In-House Reset Lifts Margins
events.body: First full quarter under fully in-house production delivered a gross margin of 61%, up nine points from the licensing era, on revenue of $740M. Blackwood credited tighter control over the origin-standard supply chain and said reorder rates on the debut collection ran 22% above internal forecasts.

events.head: Ironcrestton Unveils Meridian Line as Blackwood Pushes Into Higher Price Tiers
events.body: Ironcrestton launched Meridian, a limited-run collection positioned above its core fine-goods range, with pieces priced 40% higher than the in-house reset debut. Thea Blackwood framed the move as 'claiming the top of the table now that we control every stitch,' citing the margin gains from pulling production in-house. Initial allocations sold through at flagship locations within days, the company said.

events.head: Kessel Drive — Built to outlast its owners
events.body: Kessel Drive cut its teeth on engines that wouldn't quit, then built whole vehicles around them. Today the range runs from a rugged everyman runabout to a hand-finished grand tourer, with power packs and battery systems that feed the lot. Their cells endure brutal cold; their cars hold the road like they own it. Owners pass the keys down a generation and find the car still eager. Engineering as inheritance, torque as a promise.

events.head: Kessel Drive Debuts Long-Range Touring Vehicle in Splashy Reveal
events.body: Kessel Drive pulled the covers off its flagship 'Meridian' touring model, paired with a new high-capacity storage cell promising 30% longer service life. CEO Dorian Brandt staged the launch before 2,000 guests, claiming pre-orders topped 6,500 units within 48 hours — the company's biggest rollout in a decade.

events.head: Kessel Drive Lands Fleet Order for Long-Range Touring Line
events.body: Kessel Drive secured a 12,000-unit order from a national coach operator for its newly launched long-range touring vehicle, its biggest single fleet commitment in years. CEO Dorian Brandt called it validation of the splashy reveal, promising first deliveries within nine months. The deal includes a multi-year service and battery-storage maintenance package.

events.head: Kessel Drive Signs $3.2 Billion National Fleet Pact for Touring and Storage Lines
events.body: The multi-year agreement pairs 18,000 long-range touring vehicles with Kessel's stationary storage units across a national courier network's depots. Dorian Brandt, flanked by press at the Halloran plant, called it 'the biggest single order in our history,' pushing the company to add a third assembly shift.

events.head: Kessel Drive Faces Regulatory Probe Into Touring-Line Storage Packs
events.body: Regulators opened a formal safety probe into the storage packs powering Kessel Drive's long-range touring line following reports of thermal incidents in fleet units. The inquiry lands weeks after the 3.2-billion national fleet pact, and CEO Dorian Brandt pledged 'full cooperation' while stopping short of any pause in deliveries. The company said it was reviewing pack data across the deployed fleet as the probe gets underway.

events.head: Kessel Drive Recalls Touring-Line Storage Packs as Probe Confirms Overheating Risk
events.body: Kessel Drive issued a recall covering an estimated 48,000 storage packs across its Touring line after regulators confirmed an overheating defect. The action threatens deliveries under the recently signed $3.2 billion national fleet pact, with CEO Dorian Brandt pledging free replacements and a redesigned pack by next quarter. Analysts flagged potential penalties tied to fleet delivery timelines.

events.head: Kessel Drive Sued as Fleet Client Alleges Breach Over Recalled Storage Packs
events.body: The national fleet operator behind Kessel Drive's $3.2 billion touring pact filed suit, alleging breach of contract and seeking damages after the overheating-driven recall grounded thousands of units. CEO Dorian Brandt vowed to fight the claim while accelerating a redesigned storage pack he said would be 'faster and safer than anything on the road.' The dispute threatens the largest deal in the company's history.

events.head: Kessel Drive Rocked as Internal Memos Suggest Storage Pack Risk Was Flagged Early
events.body: Documents surfaced in the fleet-client lawsuit indicate Kessel Drive engineers had raised overheating concerns about Touring-Line storage packs months before the recall. Dorian Brandt faces mounting pressure as regulators reopened the case to examine whether disclosures were delayed. Two additional fleet operators have signaled intent to join the litigation, and the board has commissioned an independent review.

events.head: Kessel Drive Plunges Into Quarterly Loss as Recall and Legal Costs Mount
events.body: Kessel Drive reported a $290 million quarterly loss, its first in years, as recall remediation, the fleet-client suit, and reputational damage from leaked memos hammered results. CEO Dorian Brandt conceded the touring-line storage crisis had 'cost more than we projected,' as vehicle order cancellations climbed and a regulator widened its inquiry. Management withdrew full-year guidance.

events.head: Kessel Drive Ousts Dorian Brandt as Recall Fallout Forces Boardroom Reset
events.body: Kessel Drive's board voted to remove longtime CEO Dorian Brandt after mounting recall and legal costs and revelations that storage-pack risks were flagged internally. The board named turnaround specialist Neave Corliss as chief executive, tasking her with stabilizing finances and settling the fleet-client litigation.

events.head: Kessel Drive Faces Formal Regulatory Probe Into Storage Pack Failures
events.body: Regulators opened a formal safety investigation into Kessel Drive's storage packs, seeking internal records tied to the memos that surfaced last quarter. New CEO Neave Corliss pledged full cooperation and paused two Power & Storage shipments, but the probe deepens a crisis that already cost Kessel its former chief and pushed it into loss.

events.head: Kessel Drive Unveils Sweeping Restructure, Splitting Storage Unit and Cutting 3,400 Jobs
events.body: New chief Neave Corliss announced a hard reset that carves the troubled Power & Storage division into a standalone unit and eliminates 3,400 roles, aiming for $500 million in annual cost savings. Corliss pledged an overhauled quality regime for storage packs still under regulatory probe. The move marks the boldest step yet in her bid to stabilize the loss-making automaker.

events.head: Kessel Drive Widens Recall to 620,000 Vehicles as Storage Probe Deepens
events.body: Neave Corliss confirmed the storage-pack recall has ballooned to 620,000 vehicles after regulators tied additional overheating incidents to a supplier defect, with estimated costs now topping $1.9B. Corliss vowed 'total transparency,' announcing free pack replacements and a dedicated safety command center even as the formal probe continues. It is the largest recall in the automotive house's history.

events.head: Kessel Drive Plunges Into Deep Loss as Recall and Probe Costs Overwhelm Quarter
events.body: Kessel Drive posted a quarterly loss of $1.1 billion, far wider than expected, as widening recall provisions and regulatory penalties tied to its storage packs battered the balance sheet. Neave Corliss conceded the restructure had not yet stemmed the bleeding, with vehicle deliveries down 31% and the newly split storage unit still absorbing warranty charges. The board has retained outside advisers to review financing options amid speculation over a capital raise.

events.head: Kessel Drive Faces Formal Safety Probe as Regulators Escalate Storage Failure Inquiry
events.body: The National Vehicle Safety Board opened a formal investigation into thermal faults in Kessel Drive's Volt-Series storage packs, citing 14 field incidents tied to the units already under recall. CEO Neave Corliss pledged 'full cooperation and total transparency,' but the widening scope now covers manufacturing at both the Harlin and Demaking plants. Analysts warn the probe could freeze deliveries of the flagship line for two or more quarters.

events.head: Kessel Drive Halts Storage Production and Cuts 4,200 Jobs in Sweeping Overhaul
events.body: Neave Corliss announced a full suspension of the flagged storage line and a 4,200-headcount reduction across three plants, framing the move as a 'reset to zero' after the widening probe. The company will take an $880 million restructuring charge and pull its full-year guidance entirely. Corliss pledged a redesigned storage architecture within nine months, calling it 'the only path back.'

events.head: Kessel Drive Hit With Sweeping Shareholder Suit Over Storage Failures
events.body: A consolidated shareholder action filed in the Merrin district court accuses Kessel Drive of concealing known defects in its storage units months before the recall, seeking damages tied to the stock's collapse. The complaint names CEO Neave Corliss and several directors; the company said the claims are 'without merit' and vowed to defend vigorously as the parallel regulatory probe continues.

events.head: Kessel Drive Board Removes Neave Corliss as Storage Crisis Deepens
events.body: The Kessel Drive board ousted CEO Neave Corliss following the escalating safety probe, the 4,200-job overhaul, and the shareholder suit tied to storage failures. Directors appointed veteran operations chief Marta Vinke as interim CEO, pledging a full internal review of the halted storage line. The stock has shed nearly half its value since the probe opened.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. — The machine behind the machine
events.body: Kesselgrove builds industrial machines for factories that can't stop. Presses, mills, the heavy iron that runs three shifts and asks for little. The mid range earns its keep on uptime and serviceable parts; the premium line is precision-ground for plants where a thousandth of an inch is money. Engineers don't gush about it. They just keep ordering it, year after year, line after line.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Posts Quiet Record Quarter on Machine Demand
events.body: Kesselgrove reported quarterly revenue of $84 million, up 11% year-on-year, driven by orders for its precision press lines. CEO Orla Steg credited 'steady, unglamorous discipline,' adding that the order backlog now stretches into next spring.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Debuts Modular Press Platform After Quiet Development
events.body: Kesselgrove Co. revealed a modular industrial press platform that lets buyers reconfigure tooling in hours rather than days, the product of a multi-year internal program. CEO Orla Steg said early factory trials cut changeover downtime by 40 percent, positioning the platform to extend the firm's record machine-demand run.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Signs Multi-Plant Order for Modular Press Platform
events.body: Kesselgrove landed its first large deployment of the new Modular Press Platform, a 156 million agreement to outfit four fabrication plants for an industrial customer. CEO Orla Steg said the order validates the platform's quiet development phase, with initial units shipping next quarter. The deal converts the recent breakthrough into concrete revenue.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Lifts Margins as Modular Press Orders Convert to Revenue
events.body: Kesselgrove reported quarterly operating margin of 21.4%, up from 18.9% a year earlier, as multi-plant Modular Press deliveries began booking. CEO Orla Steg credited disciplined production scheduling and noted the platform's order backlog now stretches into the following fiscal year. The company reaffirmed its measured capacity-expansion plan without raising capital targets.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Adds Second Assembly Line for Modular Press Platform
events.body: With modular press orders outpacing capacity, Orla Steg approved a 95 million second assembly line at the company's main works to shorten delivery lead times. The expansion doubles annual press output and supports the multi-plant order signed last quarter. Steg said the quietly built platform has now become the company's primary growth engine.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Edges Past Estimates as Second Line Ramps Cleanly
events.body: Kesselgrove reported quarterly earnings of $3.12 a share against a $2.95 consensus, aided by faster-than-expected output from its new modular press assembly line. Steg reaffirmed full-year guidance, citing 'orderly conversion' of the multi-plant backlog.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Expands Modular Press Line With New Tooling Bay
events.body: Kesselgrove opened a dedicated tooling bay at its main plant to shorten changeover times on the modular press platform, a $31M investment. CEO Orla Steg said the addition should lift second-line output by roughly 12% while keeping the order book flowing cleanly.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Tops Estimates as New Tooling Bay Lifts Press Output
events.body: Orla Steg's firm posted a modest beat with earnings of $148 million as the modular press platform's new tooling bay came online without disruption. Utilization across both assembly lines reached 88%. Steg kept guidance steady and reiterated a preference for measured, self-funded growth.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Nudges Past Estimates as Tooling Bay Output Holds Steady
events.body: Kesselgrove Co. reported quarterly results modestly ahead of expectations, with the new tooling bay sustaining the press-line gains flagged last quarter. Orla Steg held guidance unchanged, citing 'consistent, undramatic execution.' Margins ticked up 40 basis points on improved tooling utilization.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Clears Estimates Again as Press Backlog Extends
events.body: Kesselgrove edged past forecasts as modular press orders pushed the backlog to a record 11 months. CEO Orla Steg said the tooling bay is now running at full utilization, with margins steady as pricing held firm against input costs.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Edges Estimates as Press Backlog Holds Firm
events.body: Orla Steg reported another modest beat, with press output steady and the order backlog now stretching 11 months. Margins ticked up slightly on improved tooling-bay throughput. Steg offered no change to the company's understated outlook.

events.head: Kesselgrove Co. Tops Estimates Again as Press Backlog Stretches Into Next Year
events.body: Kesselgrove Co. edged past forecasts with $610 million in revenue, extending its streak of steady quarters as its industrial press backlog now reaches into the following fiscal year. Orla Steg said tooling bay utilization held near capacity and declined to raise guidance, keeping to the firm's measured tone.

events.head: Korrgrave Mfg. — Feeding the season, every season
events.body: Korrgrove has had dirt under its fingernails since the first plow season. It supplies farm inputs across the spread, from the basics that fill every barn to the premium blends agronomists swear by. Value sacks keep small holdings solvent; the mid and top grades push yield where margins are thin. Generations of growers have planted on its word. Practical, weathered, and trusted from the gate to the granary.

events.head: Korrgrave Mfg. Adds Acreage to Northern Input Plant
events.body: Korrgrave broke ground on a modest extension to its Hartwell fertilizer works, adding capacity for the coming planting cycle. CEO Aurelia Halloran described the move as 'one more season's worth of certainty for the growers who count on us.'

events.head: Korrgrave Mfg. Nudges Past Estimates as Northern Plant Ramps
events.body: Korrgrave reported quarterly revenue of $412M, a touch above forecasts, as the recently expanded northern input plant began contributing volume. CEO Aurelia Halloran credited steady seasonal ordering and cautioned that full capacity gains would arrive gradually. Margins held flat against input costs.

events.head: Korrgrave Mfg. Delivers Steady Gains as Northern Plant Reaches Full Output
events.body: Korrgrave posted a modest 4% rise in seasonal input sales, with the expanded Northern facility now running at full capacity ahead of the planting window. CEO Aurelia Halloran characterized the results as 'exactly on plan,' declining to raise guidance.

events.head: Korrgrave Posts Steady Gains as Northern Plant Holds Full Output
events.body: Korrgrave Mfg. delivered a small earnings beat, with farm-input volumes from its Northern plant holding at full output for a second straight quarter. Chief executive Aurelia Halloran pointed to stable input costs and long-term supply contracts as the drivers of 'unremarkable but reliable' growth. Management guided for flat-to-modest gains into next season.

events.head: Korrgrave Mfg. Extends Steady Streak as Northern Plant Sustains Output
events.body: Korrgrave delivered another modest beat, with revenue up 4% as the Northern plant held full utilization for a fourth straight quarter. Aurelia Halloran credited disciplined input costs and steady farm-belt demand. The agriculture house reaffirmed its unhurried, full-year guidance.

events.head: Korrgrave Mfg. Breaks Ground on Modest Southern Blending Line
events.body: Korrgrave confirmed a $46M expansion adding a blending line at its southern facility, its first meaningful capacity addition in over a decade. CEO Aurelia Halloran framed the move as 'a careful step,' noting output would ramp gradually over three years to meet steady demand from regional cooperatives.

events.head: Korrworks — Heavy lifting, handled
events.body: Korrworks moves what others struggle to move. Material handling is the whole trade here: lifts, conveyors, the rugged gear that keeps a warehouse breathing. The mid range is the workhorse of busy docks; the premium line carries the load capacities and safety margins that big operations demand. Foremen plan their floors around it. Reliable under weight, and quietly proud of never being the thing that breaks down.

events.head: Korrworks Wins Port Authority Handling Contract
events.body: Korrworks secured a contract to supply forklifts and conveyor systems to the Brevald Port Authority, valued at an estimated $22 million over three years. CEO Rhys Throne said the win positions the company to bid on two adjacent terminal upgrades expected next year.

events.head: Korrworks Opens Second Handling Depot Near Brae Harbor
events.body: Korrworks broke ground on a 40,000-square-meter handling depot adjacent to the Brae Harbor freight corridor, expanding capacity to serve its new Port Authority contract. CEO Rhys Throne said the facility will add 220 jobs and shorten turnaround times on bulk transfers by an estimated third once operational next year.

events.head: Korrworks Signs Regional Handling Deal With Rail Operator Merrick Line
events.body: Korrworks secured a five-year contract to manage material handling across four Merrick Line freight terminals, its first move into rail-adjacent logistics. CEO Rhys Throne said the agreement, worth an estimated $210M over its term, dovetails with the recently opened Brae Harbor depot to form a connected coastal-to-inland corridor.

events.head: Korrworks Beats Estimates as New Depots and Rail Deal Lift Volumes
events.body: Korrworks posted quarterly revenue of 312 million, up 18 percent, crediting the Merrick Line agreement and the Brae Harbor depot ramp. Rhys Throne said handling throughput hit a record 4.1 million units, with the Port Authority contract now fully operational. Management raised full-year guidance modestly.

events.head: Korrworks Extends Merrick Line Pact to Cover Third Depot
events.body: Korrworks widened its handling agreement with rail operator Merrick Line, adding its newest Brae Harbor depot to the arrangement for an estimated $1.4B over six years. Rhys Throne said the expansion locks in throughput across all three depots and positions the network for a fourth site under review. The deal takes effect next quarter.

events.head: Korrworks Lifts Full-Year View as Merrick Line Volumes Compound
events.body: Handling throughput across the three-depot Merrick network rose 11 percent, prompting CEO Rhys Throne to raise annual guidance for the second time this year. Throne flagged early talks to add automated sortation at the newest depot, calling the rail pact 'a platform, not a ceiling.'

events.head: Korrworks Opens Fourth Depot as Merrick Line Corridor Reaches Capacity
events.body: Korrworks confirmed the launch of a fourth depot at Halden Junction, adding 340,000 square feet of handling capacity along the Merrick Line corridor. CEO Rhys Throne framed the move as 'seizing a corridor that keeps filling faster than we can build,' noting the new site is already 60% pre-committed to existing rail volumes. The company expects the depot to reach full throughput within two quarters.

events.head: Korrworks Lands Landmark Cross-Region Handling Pact Beyond Merrick Corridor
events.body: Korrworks signed a $1.4-billion multi-year Material Handling agreement extending its network into two new regional corridors, its largest contract to date and a decisive move past its Merrick concentration. CEO Rhys Throne called it 'the diversification we've been building toward for a decade,' with depot buildout to follow across three fresh sites.

events.head: Korrworks Breaks Ground on Cross-Region Hub to Support Landmark Handling Pact
events.body: Following its recent cross-region deal, Korrworks committed $310M to a new central sorting hub sized for volumes beyond the Merrick corridor. CEO Rhys Throne called the facility 'the backbone of the next decade,' projecting it to reach full throughput within two years.

events.head: Korrworks Signs Second Anchor Tenant for Cross-Region Hub Before Completion
events.body: Korrworks locked in a 12-year handling agreement with distributor Halvern Freight to occupy nearly a third of its still-under-construction cross-region hub. CEO Rhys Throne said the deal, valued at roughly $680 million over its term, effectively de-risks the site before its scheduled opening. The commitment brings pre-leased capacity at the hub to 55%.

events.head: Korrworks Debuts Automated Sorting Layer at Cross-Region Hub Ahead of Opening
events.body: Korrworks unveiled a new high-throughput sorting configuration for its still-unfinished cross-region hub, promising 30% faster transfer times for its two anchor tenants. CEO Rhys Throne framed the rollout as a proof point that the facility would open 'not just on time, but ahead of its class.' Full commissioning remains slated for next quarter.

events.head: Korrworks Opens Cross-Region Hub With Both Anchor Tenants Live From Day One
events.body: Korrworks cut the ribbon on its Cross-Region Hub, opening at 85% committed capacity with both anchor tenants operational and the automated sorting layer processing peak volumes on schedule. CEO Rhys Throne said day-one throughput exceeded internal projections by 12%, and hinted a fourth hub site is under evaluation. The facility supports the landmark handling pact signed last year.

events.head: Korrworks Beats as Cross-Region Hub Runs Above Plan in First Full Quarter
events.body: Rhys Throne reported the new hub processed 12% more volume than projected, lifting group revenue 9.4% with both anchor tenants at full utilization. Throne said a waitlist of secondary tenants could justify a mezzanine sorting expansion by next year. Free cash flow turned positive earlier than the completion budget forecast.

events.head: Korrworks Breaks Ground on Second Cross-Region Hub After First Runs Above Plan
events.body: Buoyed by a hub running ahead of forecast, Korrwright committed $480M to a second cross-region facility with anchor commitments already in hand. CEO Rhys Throne said the new site will carry the same automated sorting layer from day one, targeting a first-half opening next year. The company expects the two hubs together to lift throughput capacity by 60%.

events.head: Korrwright Group — Built to stand, wired to last
events.body: Korrwright Group puts up the bones and runs the nerves. It makes structural materials and the wire and cable that thread through them, supplying construction from foundation to finish. Value lines handle the volume work; the premium grades meet the codes that don't bend. Few outfits cover both the frame and the current under one roof. On a serious site, you'll likely find both stamped Korrwright.

events.head: Korrwright Group Lands Frame Contract for Verant Tower Cluster
events.body: Korrwright will supply structural beams and an estimated 4,200 miles of wire and cable for the six-tower Verant district development, a deal valued at $1.8 billion over four years. CEO Halden Fenn called the win 'the kind of anchor project that fills a decade,' noting deliveries begin next quarter. The contract edges out two rival suppliers who had held the regional account since the 1930s.

events.head: Korrwright Group Posts Strong Quarter as Verant Frame Work Begins
events.body: Korrwright reported revenue of 1.2 billion, up 14% year-on-year, with structural materials orders climbing as steel framing for the Verant Tower Cluster moved into early delivery. Halden Fenn credited disciplined input contracts and noted wire and cable backlogs now stretch eleven months. Margins widened to 18.3% on firmer pricing.

events.head: Korrwright Group Wins Full Wire-and-Cable Mandate for Verant Cluster
events.body: Building on its frame contract, Korrwright has secured the entire structural wiring and cabling package for all six Verant Tower buildings, a deal valued at roughly 480 million and stretching four years. CEO Halden Fenn called it the largest single-site award in the group's century-long history, consolidating both of Korrwright's core lines under one project. Analysts note the win effectively ties the firm's fortunes to Verant's construction timeline through 2029.

events.head: Korrwright Group Lifts Guidance as Verant Wire Mandate Feeds Backlog
events.body: Korrwright reported a 22 percent jump in structural and cable revenue to 480 million as both the frame and wire mandates at Verant advanced simultaneously. Halden Fenn said the combined Verant work now represents the largest backlog in the firm's century-long history. The board raised the dividend by 6 percent.

events.head: Korrwright Group Adds Wire Line to Keep Pace With Verant Backlog
events.body: Korrwright will commission a new high-capacity wire-drawing line at its Halden works to service the growing Verant cluster mandate, a $220M investment set to double output by year-end. Halden Fenn said the expansion answers a backlog that has stretched delivery windows, with the first spools expected within three quarters. The move follows two consecutive guidance lifts.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats as New Wire Line Clears Verant Backlog Faster
events.body: The added wire line cut Verant delivery lead times from 20 to 13 weeks, helping quarterly earnings top estimates by 6 percent. CEO Halden Fenn said the cluster mandate is now roughly 60 percent delivered, with structural-materials orders beginning to trail in behind the cable work.

events.head: Korrwright Group Signs Follow-On Wire Contract as Verant Extends Through 2031
events.body: Korrwright secured a renewal and expansion of its Verant supply arrangement valued near $210M, locking in structural-materials and wire volumes for six additional years. CEO Halden Fenn said the deal underpins utilization at the new wire line and supports a modest dividend lift. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance on the strengthened backlog.

events.head: Korrwright Group Breaks Ground on Structural Materials Plant to Anchor Verant Corridor
events.body: Korrwright committed $340 million to a new Structural Materials facility near the Verant corridor, positioning it to bundle materials with its extended wire contract through 2031. CEO Halden Fenn framed the move as 'meeting Verant where it is heading, not where it stands,' with first output slated for late next year.

events.head: Korrwright Group Opens Verant Corridor Plant, Ships First Structural Beams
events.body: The new Verant Corridor plant rolled out its first structural beam line three weeks ahead of schedule, with initial output earmarked for corridor infrastructure work. Halden Fenn said the facility would reach full capacity of 340,000 tonnes annually by mid-cycle, tightening Korrwright's grip on the region it has supplied wire to since 2028.

events.head: Korrwright Group Wins $1.4B Corridor Infrastructure Package Spanning Beams and Cable
events.body: Halden Fenn secured a $1.4 billion multi-year award to supply structural materials and wire for the next phase of the Verant Corridor buildout. The contract pairs the recently opened corridor plant with Korrwright's cable operations, locking in demand through 2032. Fenn called it validation of the vertically integrated bet the company placed on the corridor.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats as Corridor Package Drives Record Beam and Cable Shipments
events.body: Korrwright Group posted revenue of $2.1 billion, up 19%, as the $1.4B corridor infrastructure package entered peak delivery across beams and wire. CEO Halden Fenn said the Verant Corridor plant is running at 85% capacity less than a year after opening. Backlog stood at $3.6 billion, giving the company visibility into 2027.

events.head: Korrwright Group Adds Second Line at Verant Corridor Plant to Clear Backlog
events.body: Korrwright approved a $180M second production line at its Verant Corridor plant to keep pace with the $1.4B infrastructure package. CEO Halden Fenn said cable output will roughly double once the line reaches full rate next year, easing lead times that had stretched to record lengths. The expansion adds an estimated 300 jobs at the site.

events.head: Korrwright Group Lands $600M Rail-Bridge Contract to Follow Corridor Work
events.body: Korrwright Group secured a $600 million package to supply structural beams and wire assemblies for a regional rail-bridge program, extending demand well past its current Verant corridor backlog. CEO Halden Fenn said the win validates the decision to add a second line, which will now run near capacity into next year. Deliveries begin in the second half.

events.head: Korrwright Group Beats Again as Rail-Bridge Work Joins Corridor Backlog
events.body: Korrwright reported quarterly revenue of $1.4B, up 11% year over year, as the $600M rail-bridge contract began contributing alongside the ongoing corridor package. CEO Halden Fenn cited the second Verant line for holding delivery times steady despite record combined beam and cable volumes. The order book now stretches nearly two years out.

events.head: Korrwright Works Buys Heritage Dial-Maker Velloux
events.body: Dunmore Carrow added the storied dial atelier Velloux to the Korrwright stable, securing a sought-after enamel workshop. The acquisition gives Korrwright in-house control over its most coveted finishes. Carrow said he 'won't wait on suppliers for art.'

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts the Velloux Heritage Series, Its First Since the Acquisition
events.body: Korrwright Works has launched the Velloux Heritage series, a six-model line pairing its movements with enamel dials from the newly acquired Velloux workshop. CEO Dunmore Carrow positioned the collection as proof the buyout was 'about craft, not just capacity,' with pieces priced from 14,000 to 60,000. The opening run of 900 units sold through to dealers within the first week.

events.head: Korrwright Works Velloux Heritage Series Wins Carrowmore Craft Prize
events.body: The Velloux Heritage Series took top honors in the enamel-dial category at the annual Carrowmore Craft Prize, the first such recognition since Korrwright absorbed Velloux. Judges praised the restored kiln-firing technique recovered from Velloux's archives. Dunmore Carrow called the award 'proof the heritage was worth buying.'

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Velloux Dial Craft Into New Heritage Atelier
events.body: Riding three straight wins of acclaim, Dunmore Carrow has authorized a dedicated Heritage Atelier in the Carrowmore district to house Velloux's restored dial presses alongside Korrwright's master finishers. The 40,000-square-foot site will lift annual hand-finished output by roughly 18 percent and consolidate two formerly separate workshops. Carrow called it 'the natural next acquisition of space, now that we own the talent.'

events.head: Korrwright Works Secures Exclusive Movement Supply Pact for Heritage Atelier
events.body: Korrwright Works has signed a five-year exclusivity agreement with escapement specialist Loewen & Fisk, locking up rare hairspring alloys for its new Heritage Atelier at a reported 42 million per annum. CEO Dunmore Carrow called the deal 'the connective tissue between the Velloux acquisition and everything that follows,' hinting at further vertical purchases. Analysts note the pact removes a key supply bottleneck that had capped Velloux output.

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts Velloux Atelier Series, First Line From New Heritage Workshop
events.body: Korrwright Works unveiled the Velloux Atelier Series, the inaugural collection produced entirely at its recently consolidated Heritage Atelier. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the movement-supply pact secured earlier this year enabled a limited run of 1,200 pieces, each priced above the prior Heritage tier. Early demand from three key salons has already reserved half the initial allotment.

events.head: Korrwright Works' Velloux Atelier Series Named Timepiece of the Year by Chronard Guild
events.body: The debut line from Korrwright's new Heritage Atelier took top honors at the Chronard Guild awards, with judges praising the revived Velloux dial craft. Chief executive Dunmore Carrow said the recognition 'validates every acquisition we've made to bring this workshop under one roof.'

events.head: Korrwright Works Buys Rival Heritage Maker Sennfeld in Landmark Deal
events.body: Dunmore Carrow announced the $2.1B acquisition of storied competitor Sennfeld Chronometers, folding its ateliers and movement archive into the Velloux operation. The purchase, Korrwright's largest ever, doubles its skilled watchmaker headcount and secures a century of proprietary complications. Carrow said the combined house would 'define the top of the market,' capping a run that began with the Velloux launch and its Timepiece of the Year win.

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Sennfeld Atelier Into Unified Heritage Division
events.body: Dunmore Carrow announced Sennfeld's storied workshop will be merged into a single Korrwright Heritage Division, consolidating three ateliers and cutting an estimated 140 back-office roles. Carrow framed the move as 'protecting two centuries of craft under one roof,' though guild observers noted the pace of integration has unsettled Sennfeld's veteran finishers.

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts Sennfeld Revival Line Under Unified Heritage Division
events.body: The luxury timepiece maker unveiled the Sennfeld Revival, a 12-model collection blending the acquired atelier's tourbillon craft with Korrwright's Velloux movement, priced from 38,000. CEO Dunmore Carrow called the launch 'proof the folding-in worked,' with initial allocations already committed to flagship boutiques in three markets.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Sennfeld Revival Line Drives Heritage Division Sales
events.body: Quarterly revenue rose 14% to $612 million, powered by strong early demand for the Sennfeld Revival timepieces launched under the unified Heritage Division. CEO Dunmore Carrow said waitlists on flagship models had cleared expectations and hinted at further acquisitions in the coming year. Margins widened as integration savings from the Sennfeld deal began to land.

events.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Vellhorn Movements to Secure In-House Escapements
events.body: Korrwright Works announced the 340 million-crown purchase of Vellhorn Movements, a specialist escapement maker, bringing a key supplier under the Unified Heritage Division. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the deal 'ends our dependence on outside calibers' and will feed directly into the expanding Sennfeld Revival line.

events.head: Korrwright Works Unveils First Timepieces Built on In-House Vellhorn Escapements
events.body: Korrwright debuted its Meridian collection, the first line to feature escapements from the recently acquired Vellhorn Movements, priced from $8,400. CEO Dunmore Carrow said full vertical integration cuts reliance on outside suppliers and improves margins on the heritage division's flagship pieces. Initial allocations to boutiques are already spoken for.

events.head: Korrwright Works Seals $1.2B Takeover of Heritage Rival Ambrose & Sons
events.body: In his boldest move in decades, Dunmore Carrow has agreed to acquire storied competitor Ambrose & Sons for $1.2 billion, folding its two-century dial-making workshops and prestige boutiques into the Korrwright stable. The deal doubles Korrwright's atelier capacity and adds the coveted Ambrose Meridian collection, though analysts note Carrow now faces the challenge of integrating three heritage brands at once. Regulators in two markets are expected to review the combination over the coming months.

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Ambrose & Sons Into New Heritage Division
events.body: Following its $1.2B takeover, Korrwright Works announced it will consolidate Ambrose & Sons and the acquired Vellhorn movements arm under a single Heritage Division led from the Carrow flagship workshop. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the reorganization will trim roughly 260 overlapping roles while preserving Ambrose's landmark casing atelier. The firm expects $90M in annual cost savings from combined escapement production by the second year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Heritage Division Lifts Margins
events.body: Korrwright reported a 14% revenue rise, with the newly folded Ambrose & Sons operations contributing ahead of internal targets in their first full quarter. CEO Dunmore Carrow credited shared Vellhorn escapement tooling for cutting per-unit costs across both brands. Management hinted that integration savings would free capital for further acquisitions.

events.head: Korrwright Works Opens Flagship Heritage Atelier as Carrow Eyes New Markets
events.body: Dunmore Carrow cut the ribbon on a restored downtown atelier that consolidates Korrwright and Ambrose & Sons craftsmanship under one roof, adding roughly 120 master watchmakers. The 40,000-square-foot facility is expected to lift annual output of high-complication timepieces by nearly a third. Carrow hinted the site is a launchpad for entry into two overseas luxury markets next year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Seizes Rival Meridienne in $2.4B Cross-Border Coup
events.body: Dunmore Carrow moved on longtime competitor Meridienne Horlogerie, acquiring the storied movement-house for $2.4 billion in the largest deal of his 118-year tenure. The purchase hands the new Heritage Division control of Meridienne's celebrated tourbillon workshops and opens the eastern markets Carrow had publicly targeted. Executives said Meridienne's 340 master watchmakers will be retained under the Korrwright banner.

events.head: Korrwright Works Folds Meridienne Into New 'Korrwright Meridienne' Luxury House
events.body: Korrwright Works unveiled a unified luxury identity, rebranding its acquired rival under the combined 'Korrwright Meridienne' banner to consolidate heritage collections under one crest. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the merged house would share ateliers while preserving Meridienne's signature movements. Management expects the rebrand to lift blended margins as duplicate distribution costs are stripped out.

events.head: Korrwright Works Slips as Meridienne Integration Costs Bite
events.body: Quarterly earnings came in 11% below expectations as the $2.4B Meridienne acquisition dragged margins with duplicated overhead and rebranding spend. Dunmore Carrow acknowledged 'a heavier lift than modeled' but insisted the combined Korrwright Meridienne house would deliver by next fiscal year. Integration charges totaled $310M, the bulk tied to consolidating two overlapping atelier networks.

events.head: Korrwright Works Reopens Meridienne Salon in Grand Relaunch as Integration Costs Ease
events.body: With the worst of the merger charges behind it, Korrwright Works has poured $180M into refurbishing the flagship Korrwright Meridienne salon, restoring the acquired workshops to full craft capacity. CEO Dunmore Carrow framed the relaunch as 'the payoff phase,' telling reporters the combined house now spans two centuries of horological heritage under one roof.

events.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Reopened Meridienne Salon Drives Luxury Demand
events.body: Quarterly revenue rose 11% to $482M as the relaunched Meridienne salon posted record footfall and higher average ticket prices on limited-run timepieces. Dunmore Carrow credited the integration for lifting group margins back above 28%, reversing the prior quarter's slip. The house said waitlists for its flagship complications now stretch into next year.

events.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Heritage Movement Maker Alvence in $340M Deal
events.body: Korrwright Works has agreed to buy movement specialist Alvence for $340 million, extending CEO Dunmore Carrow's acquisitive streak on the back of the Meridienne salon's revival. The purchase secures in-house mechanical calibers that had previously been sourced externally, echoing rivals' move toward vertical integration. Carrow said Alvence's workshops will supply the reopened Meridienne line first.

events.head: Korrwright Works Debuts Alvence-Built In-House Movement in Meridienne Flagship
events.body: Five months after the $340M Alvence acquisition, Korrwright unveiled the Meridienne Calibre 12, its first timepiece using a fully in-house movement from the Alvence workshops. CEO Dunmore Carrow priced the debut edition at $58,000 and capped the first run at 400 pieces, saying vertical control of movements ends the house's reliance on outside suppliers. Early salon allocations reportedly cleared within days of the private preview.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Folds Voss Cell Into New Power & Storage Division
events.body: Following its $6.4B acquisition, Lhaus Industries announced it will consolidate Voss Cell operations into a dedicated Power & Storage unit led out of the Ferrlands campus. CEO Cole Brandt said the reorganization would cut roughly 900 overlapping roles but retain Voss Cell's core cell-chemistry team, targeting $340M in annual synergies by 1955.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Unveils First Cell Pack From New Power & Storage Division
events.body: Lhaus rolled out the Voss-badged HX series, its first storage product engineered since folding in the acquired unit. CEO Cole Brandt said the pack targets fleet and grid buyers and that a driveline-integrated variant is already in testing at Ferrlands. Initial shipments are slated for two regional distributors.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Lands $9B Fleet Supply Pact for New Cell Packs
events.body: Cole Brandt secured a landmark five-year agreement to supply cell packs from the newly formed Power & Storage division to a major commercial fleet operator, valued at up to $9B. The deal validates the $6.4B Voss Cell acquisition and positions Lhaus as a top-tier supplier beyond its traditional auto-parts base. Brandt said the division was already fielding inquiries that could double its order book by year-end.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Breaks Ground on Dedicated Cell-Pack Plant to Feed $9B Fleet Pact
events.body: Lhaus committed $1.6B to a new Power & Storage facility at Merrow Bend, designed to produce 30 GWh of cell packs annually once fully online in 2028. CEO Cole Brandt said the plant would secure supply for the recently signed fleet pact and 'leave room for the next three deals we haven't announced yet.' The site is expected to add roughly 900 jobs.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Debuts Fast-Charge Cell Pack With Record Cycle Life
events.body: Lhaus unveiled a second-generation cell pack it says retains 90% capacity after 4,000 cycles while accepting an 80% charge in under twelve minutes. Chief engineer Marta Voss said the breakthrough came from a new electrode chemistry developed at the company's Fenwick lab, and Cole Brandt hinted the technology could underpin a broader push beyond fleet customers. Analysts called it the most significant Power & Storage advance since the division launched.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Signs $14B Second Fleet Pact on Strength of Fast-Charge Packs
events.body: Building on its record cycle-life breakthrough, Lhaus landed a 14-billion-mark, seven-year agreement to supply cell packs to a major commercial hauler consortium. Cole Brandt said the win validates the dedicated cell-pack plant now nearing completion, and confirmed Lhaus will break ground on a second facility to meet combined demand from both fleet contracts.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Adds Third Cell-Pack Line as Fleet Backlog Swells to $23B
events.body: Cole Brandt announced a $2.1B expansion of the flagship cell-pack complex, adding a third line to keep pace with a combined fleet backlog now topping $23B across two pacts. The restless chief also confirmed talks to acquire a regional power-storage supplier, saying Lhaus 'cannot build fast enough' to meet demand. The new line is expected to reach volume output within 14 months.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Clinches $31B Cell-Pack Deal, Its Largest Ever
events.body: Lhaus signed a supply-and-licensing pact valued at up to $31B to furnish fast-charge cell packs to a coalition of regional transit operators, lifting its total backlog past $54B. Brandt said the agreement 'locks in a decade of demand' and would require a fourth production line to be announced within months.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Breaks Ground on Fourth Cell-Pack Line to Clear Record Backlog
events.body: Lhaus began construction on a fourth cell-pack line at its Torren works, a $1.8B investment aimed at servicing a backlog that has swelled past $50B after its record deal. CEO Cole Brandt said the added capacity would 'take delivery risk off the table' for fleet customers waiting into next year. The line is targeted to reach volume output within 14 months.

events.head: Lhaus Misses as Fourth-Line Startup Costs Bite Into Margins
events.body: Lhaus fell short of estimates despite record revenue, as commissioning costs for its fourth cell-pack line compressed margins to 8.2% from 12.5% a year earlier. CEO Cole Brandt defended the aggressive buildout, insisting the $31B backlog justifies near-term pain. Analysts flagged rising leverage as Lhaus stacks capacity faster than deliveries convert to cash.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Rebounds as Fourth Cell-Pack Line Reaches Full Output
events.body: Lhaus topped estimates with revenue of $9.8 billion, as the fourth cell-pack line ramped to full capacity and startup costs that dented prior margins rolled off. CEO Cole Brandt said the record backlog behind the $31B deal is now clearing 'faster than modeled,' with operating margin recovering to 14%. The company reaffirmed plans to evaluate a fifth line.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Acquires Rival Cell-Pack Maker Delphin in $6.4 Billion Deal
events.body: Lhaus agreed to buy fellow supplier Delphin Systems for $6.4 billion, its largest acquisition in two decades, folding four additional cell-pack facilities into a network already running near capacity. CEO Cole Brandt framed the purchase as a way to 'stop building lines one at a time,' and said combined output should clear the standing backlog by next year, pending regulatory review.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Folds Delphin Plants Into Unified Cell-Pack Network
events.body: Cole Brandt confirmed the integration of Delphin's three facilities alongside Lhaus's own four lines, creating a combined footprint the company says will lift annual cell-pack output by 42 percent. The consolidation will center operations at the expanded Harrowgate campus, with Brandt naming Delphin's former operations head Ilse Marren to run the merged unit. Management reaffirmed cost-synergy targets of $310 million by 2028.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Breaks Ground on Fifth Cell-Pack Line as Brandt Chases Scale
events.body: Fresh off absorbing Delphin's plants, Cole Brandt announced a $2.1 billion investment to add a fifth cell-pack line at the newly unified Halbrook complex. The move lifts targeted annual output past 40 gigawatt-hours and, Brandt told reporters, positions Lhaus to underbid rivals on volume contracts. Analysts noted the pace reflects Brandt's long habit of building faster than demand strictly requires.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Misses as Cell-Pack Buildout Costs Squeeze Margins
events.body: Lhaus reported quarterly profit below expectations as the rapid Delphin integration and fifth-line construction pushed capital spending and startup costs higher than guided. Margins in the cell-pack segment slipped to 9.1% from 13.4% a year earlier, though Cole Brandt insisted the scale push would pay off once new lines reach full run-rate. Vehicle and parts units held steady.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Pauses Sixth Cell-Pack Line, Trims Buildout to Protect Margins
events.body: Following last quarter's earnings miss, Lhaus announced it will delay its planned sixth cell-pack line and consolidate two underused Delphin sub-assemblies, targeting $180 million in annualized savings. CEO Cole Brandt said the moves would 'let the existing five lines earn their keep' before further expansion. The company maintained its full-year volume outlook but conceded margin recovery would take two to three quarters.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Returns to a Beat as Trimmed Buildout Restores Margins
events.body: After two rough quarters, Lhaus topped estimates as the paused sixth-line spend fell out of the cost base and the five running cell-pack lines reached target yields. CEO Cole Brandt said free cash flow turned positive again and hinted the sixth line could restart 'once the numbers earn it,' signaling his acquisitive streak isn't fully cooled.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Restarts Sixth Cell-Pack Line as Brandt Eyes Storage Push
events.body: With margins stabilized, CEO Cole Brandt greenlit the resumption of the previously paused sixth cell-pack line, backed by a $420 million capital commitment. Brandt framed the move as a return to offense, targeting a 30% lift in Power & Storage output by next year to chase surging grid-storage demand.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Secures $2.8B Grid-Storage Supply Pact in Landmark Storage Pivot
events.body: Cole Brandt landed a multi-year agreement to supply cell packs for a national grid-storage operator, validating the restarted sixth line and the broader storage push. The deal, worth up to $2.8B over six years, marks Lhaus's largest single contract outside automotive parts. Brandt called it 'the transformation we restarted that line for.'

events.head: Lhaus Industries Breaks Ground on Dedicated Grid-Storage Plant to Serve $2.8B Pact
events.body: Lhaus committed $640 million to a purpose-built cell-pack facility in Vantmoor, its first plant devoted entirely to grid-storage output under the landmark supply pact. Cole Brandt said the site will run four assembly lines at launch with room to double, easing pressure on the six retrofitted automotive lines. Initial deliveries from the plant are targeted within 18 months.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Seals Second Grid-Storage Megadeal Worth $3.4B, Cementing Storage Pivot
events.body: Lhaus stunned the sector by landing a $3.4B, seven-year grid-storage supply agreement with a consortium of utilities, its largest contract ever and second major storage win in under a year. CEO Cole Brandt said the deal validates the pivot away from legacy auto parts and pledged to fast-track a second dedicated storage plant. Combined storage backlog now exceeds $6B.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Faces Regulatory Probe After Grid-Storage Overheating Reports
events.body: Regulators opened a formal safety review into Lhaus Industries' grid-storage units following three reported thermal incidents at customer sites tied to its $2.8 billion pact. The probe casts a shadow over Cole Brandt's aggressive storage pivot, with the second $3.4 billion megadeal now under contractual review. Brandt said the company is 'cooperating fully' and has paused shipments from the new dedicated plant pending inspection.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Recalls Grid-Storage Units Across Two Megadeals as Probe Confirms Overheating Fault
events.body: Lhaus issued a recall covering roughly 60,000 grid-storage modules delivered under its $2.8B and $3.4B pacts after regulators confirmed a thermal-management defect behind earlier overheating reports. Cole Brandt said both anchor buyers were notified and that the dedicated storage plant would shift to a corrected design, at an estimated $320 million cost. The company said it aims to preserve delivery commitments but flagged possible schedule slippage on the second megadeal.

events.head: Lhaus Industries Sued for $1.8B as Grid-Storage Partners Allege Concealed Overheating Data
events.body: Two megadeal counterparties filed a joint $1.8B suit claiming Lhaus withheld internal thermal-test findings before signing the grid-storage contracts. The complaint alleges CEO Cole Brandt's team accelerated deployments despite known fault margins, deepening the fallout from last quarter's recall. Lhaus called the claims 'without merit' but disclosed it has set aside $400M in reserves.

events.head: Maison & Vale — Order, in every quiet detail
events.body: Maison & Vale brought a touch of grace to the workaday business of keeping house. Their cleaning supplies, janitorial lines, and household goods marry function with a finish you'd actually want on display. The value range earns its place in everyday cupboards; the mid tier dresses boutique stays and well-run homes. There's a pleasing weight to their wares, a sense someone cared. Tidiness raised, gently, to something close to a small pleasure.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Cleaning-Supply Maker Sundle Werks
events.body: The hospitality group has purchased Sundle Werks, a mid-sized jansan manufacturer, for $340 million, folding its detergent and sanitizer lines into Maison & Vale's household catalog. Restless as ever, CEO Rhys Kessler framed the buy as 'closing the last gap between our front desks and our supply closets.' The deal adds three plants and roughly 900 workers.

events.head: Maison & Vale Rolls Out Sundle-Branded Professional Cleaning Range
events.body: Following its Sundle Werks acquisition, Maison & Vale launched a 14-product professional cleaning line aimed at hotels and serviced residences. CEO Rhys Kessler said the range pairs Sundle's formulations with Maison & Vale's hospitality distribution. Initial rollout targets the company's existing managed-property clients.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Household-Goods Maker Corran Linens
events.body: Rhys Kessler added Corran Linens in a $310 million deal, broadening the group beyond cleaning into premium household textiles. Kessler said the purchase 'completes the room,' pairing Sundle's professional supplies with Corran's linens under a single hospitality banner.

events.head: Maison & Vale Lands Continental Hotel-Group Supply Deal for Combined Portfolio
events.body: Rhys Kessler unveiled a five-year, 340 million-unit supply agreement to stock cleaning and household lines across the Meridian Suites chain's 1,200 properties, marrying the freshly integrated Sundle Werks and Corran Linens ranges under one contract. Kessler said the pact validates his rapid acquisition spree, projecting the deal alone would add roughly 18% to annual revenue. Analysts noted it is the largest single order in the company's 86-year history.

events.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Corran Linens and Hotel Deal Boost Combined Portfolio
events.body: Maison & Vale posted revenue of $760M, up 19%, with the Corran Linens acquisition and continental hotel-group supply deal both contributing ahead of plan. CEO Rhys Kessler said cross-selling the Sundle cleaning range into household-goods accounts drove margin gains and signaled appetite for further bolt-on buys. Household Goods is now the fastest-growing segment.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Jansan Supplier Deltrey Chemical to Deepen Portfolio
events.body: Restless dealmaker Rhys Kessler struck again, agreeing to buy cleaning-products maker Deltrey Chemical for 620 million to lock in supply for the Continental hotel contract. The deal adds industrial sanitation lines that Maison & Vale previously sourced externally, and Kessler said it should lift combined margins by roughly two points within a year. Integration will fold Deltrey's two plants into the existing Corran Linens operations network.

events.head: Maison & Vale Seals $2.2-Billion Merger With Rival Ostley Hospitality Group
events.body: In its most ambitious move yet, the house agreed to combine with cleaning-and-household rival Ostley in a deal valuing the target at $2.2 billion, creating the continent's largest jansan and household-goods supplier. CEO Rhys Kessler said Deltrey Chemical and Corran Linens would be folded alongside Ostley's brands, though regulators in two regions signaled early scrutiny of the combined market share.

events.head: Maison & Vale Misses as Ostley Merger Costs Weigh on Margins
events.body: Integration expenses from the $2.2-billion Ostley tie-up pushed quarterly profit 14% below expectations, despite revenue climbing to 1.9 billion marks. Kessler acknowledged the merger was 'proving heavier to digest than modeled' but defended the combined footprint. Overlapping Jansan operations from the Deltrey acquisition added to near-term redundancy costs.

events.head: Maison & Vale Folds Deltrey and Ostley Units Into Streamlined Jansan Division
events.body: Seeking to stem the margin pressure that dragged on last quarter, Maison & Vale consolidated Deltrey Chemical and legacy Ostley operations into a single Jansan division, cutting an estimated 900 overlapping roles. CEO Rhys Kessler said the reorganization targets $180 million in annual savings and should restore margins by mid-year.

events.head: Maison & Vale Returns to Growth as Streamlined Jansan Division Lifts Margins
events.body: Maison & Vale reported quarterly operating margin recovery to 11.2%, up from 7.4%, as the consolidated Jansan division began delivering the synergies promised in the Ostley deal. CEO Rhys Kessler credited '$140 million in annualized cost savings' from folding the Deltrey and Ostley units together. Household Goods volumes also stabilized after two soft quarters.

events.head: Maison & Vale Acquires Household-Goods Maker Calbrook in $1.8 Billion Deal
events.body: Rhys Kessler, restless after finally stabilizing margins, announced the $1.8 billion purchase of Calbrook, a mid-market household-goods brand, to broaden the portfolio beyond the streamlined jansan division. Kessler framed the deal as 'the next leg,' pledging to avoid the integration costs that dragged the earlier Ostley merger. Investors watched warily given Maison & Vale's recent margin scare.

events.head: Maison & Vale Merges Calbrook Into Household-Goods Arm as Kessler Cuts Overlap
events.body: Rhys Kessler folded the $1.8 billion Calbrook purchase into a newly consolidated Household Goods Group, eliminating roughly 600 duplicated back-office roles and shuttering two aging plants. Kessler said the reorganization should deliver $140 million in annual savings by next fiscal year. The move mirrors last year's Jansan streamlining that returned the company to growth.

events.head: Maison & Vale Strikes $3.2 Billion Deal for Cleaning-Chemicals Giant Northram
events.body: Fresh off digesting Calbrook, Rhys Kessler unveiled the acquisition of Northram Solutions, a jansan-chemicals maker with 4,000 employees, in a $3.2 billion cash-and-stock deal. The purchase nearly doubles the Cleaning & Jansan division's revenue base, though analysts flagged integration risk given the back-to-back dealmaking pace.

events.head: Maison & Vale Folds Northram Into Cleaning Arm as Kessler Chases $400M in Savings
events.body: Rhys Kessler moved swiftly to integrate the $3.2 billion Northram acquisition, merging its chemicals operations into Maison & Vale's cleaning-and-jansan division and targeting $400 million in annual synergies. The plan consolidates three plants and trims overlapping distribution routes, with roughly 900 roles affected. Kessler framed the move as necessary discipline after a rapid stretch of dealmaking.

events.head: Maison & Vale Beats as Northram Integration Delivers Early Savings
events.body: Maison & Vale reported quarterly operating income of $1.9 billion, ahead of the $1.7 billion consensus, crediting $180 million in realized synergies from the folded-in Northram cleaning arm. Rhys Kessler said the integration is 'ahead of schedule' toward the $400 million savings target and hinted at further consolidation across the Jansan portfolio.

events.head: Maison & Vale Adds Household-Goods Maker Corriveau in $1.1B Bolt-On
events.body: Fresh off the Northram integration, restless CEO Rhys Kessler struck a $1.1 billion cash-and-stock deal for household-goods maker Corriveau, extending Maison & Vale beyond cleaning chemicals into shelf-stable home products. Kessler said the acquisition unlocks shared distribution with Northram and targets a further $150 million in combined savings by 2028. Regulators are expected to clear the deal within two quarters.

events.head: Marlgear Supply — Smart iron for working floors
events.body: Marlgear Supply sits where the wrench meets the circuit. It builds devices and industrial machines for operations that want their tools to think a little. The value range gets the job done without fuss; the premium line packs the sensors and durability that modern plants lean on. Newer than the old iron houses and faster on its feet, it has earned a name for gear that's clever where it counts.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Unveils the Atlas Industrial Press
events.body: Halden Vossen made a splash at the Ironworks Expo with the Atlas, a heavy industrial press he claims halves changeover time on the factory floor. Vossen ran a live stamping demo and took open questions for an hour. The bold showing positions Marlgear as more than a devices maker.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Books First Atlas Order From Drennan Mills
events.body: Marlgear Supply secured its first major Atlas press order from Drennan Mills, a sizable fabricator in the southern works belt. Halden Vossen said the deal validates the firm's leap into industrial machines. Delivery is slated across two phases this year.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Lands Landmark Atlas Order From Carrow Group
events.body: Marlgear signed a £240 million framework with manufacturing conglomerate Carrow Group to supply 90 Atlas Industrial Presses across eleven plants over three years, the largest order in the company's history. Halden Vossen called it 'the day the working floor changed hands,' staking Marlgear's expansion plans on the deal. Shares of the Drennan Mills supply chain are expected to ramp through next quarter.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Posts Record Quarter as Atlas Backlog Swells
events.body: Marlgear reported quarterly revenue of 1.2 billion, up 31% year over year, driven entirely by Atlas Industrial Press demand from the Drennan and Carrow contracts. The order backlog now stretches 14 months, prompting CEO Halden Vossen to declare the press line 'the most important machine we have ever built.' Vossen also teased a second assembly site to ease the bottleneck.

events.head: Marlgear Supply Faces Regulatory Probe Over Atlas Machine Failures at Drennan Mills
events.body: A safety authority opened a formal investigation into Marlgear Supply's flagship Atlas industrial machines after three reported mechanical failures at Drennan Mills, one causing a serious floor injury.
